next_action_hypothesis: The three-strategy approved-target budget is exhausted. If the work area is reopened under a new target episode, shift or reduce the camera-facing roof so the blue/cream tool board, separated large tools, bench and vise become the first read beneath visibly supported cover; restore material contrast between roof and work surface.

observations.art_direction_fit: Timber and sheet construction suggest salvage, but the pale roof/bench treatment and shelter-first silhouette weaken the approved Scavenger hand-work target.
observations.close_up_quality: The close proxy confirms roof and bench construction, but Luna still cannot recover the hand-work function or tool-board read.
observations.gameplay_readability: Luna scores work-area identity 1/5, bench/vise visibility 2/5, and tool-board/tool visibility 1/5 at the controlled 64-inch Room A camera.
observations.geometric_detail: The close three-quarter capture shows a modeled bench, roof panels, posts and braces, but most work details disappear from the 64-inch views.
observations.material_realism: The alternate solid color blocks make the roof bright white/salmon and the bench pale; Luna rates their separation 2/5.
observations.proportion: The bench and tool board occupy too little visible area under the wide bright canopy; the front canopy still takes visual priority.
observations.scale_fidelity: Godot reports bounds 22.81 x 8.045 x 10.03 inches against the 23 x 9 x 12 inch brief.
observations.semantic_recognizability: Luna identifies the 64-inch read as a canopy shelter; neither the tool board nor large hand tools establish the work-area function.
observations.silhouette_quality: The broad roof remains the dominant shape in the Room A 64-inch front, opposite and side captures.
observations.surface_variation: Removing the baked patina maps leaves broad roof and bench surfaces visually even at the close camera proxy.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 imports and validates the review-only GLB through the Room A production scene; gameplay contracts remain separate.

close_inspection.evidence: At the close camera proxy, broad smooth roof and bench materials lack enough surface separation, while the tool board and large hand tools remain occluded from the observed angle.

edge_treatment.evidence: The close three-quarter capture shows sheet edges, bench thickness and timber post sections.

hardware.evidence: The Room A 64-inch images do not resolve the hand vise into readable hardware, and no other clear work-hardware focal point is visible.

joins.evidence: Cross headers, roof purlins, knee braces and posts form a visible supported canopy in the close capture.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: At the 64-inch camera, the board-mounted tool layout, vise and hand-work arrangement do not communicate a manufactured work bay.

material_response.evidence: The solid material blocks render roof and bench as similarly pale surfaces; their separation is weak in the Room A scene.

surface_variation.evidence: Broad white and salmon roof panels and the pale bench have little visible wear variation after the alternate strategy removed baked maps.

thickness.evidence: The roof sheets and workbench top have visible thickness in the close capture.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: The close three-quarter production capture reads as a constructed timber and sheet-metal shelter with a bench, though the work-area identity does not survive at 64 inches.

photo_character.evidence: The ArtBrief does not require photographic-source character or list reference images.

visual_transfer_diagnosis.corrective_action: Backlog the current target after three strategies. A future target should expose the tool board and bench beneath a smaller or camera-shifted canopy while restoring clear roof-to-bench material contrast.
